scholarships.title: Cusanuswerk Promotionsstipendium (Auswahlverfahren für Promovierende) — Cusanuswerk Doctoral Scholarship

existing.description: The Cusanuswerk is the talent development body of the Catholic Church in Germany and funds doctoral candidates through its Promotionsförderung. The current round (Verfahren I-2027) accepts registrations until 1 November 2026 with a selection decision in March 2027. Funding is a parent-independent stipend of EUR 1,750 plus a EUR 100 research cost allowance, with optional health-insurance, child-care and family supplements and possible support for research stays abroad; the official page states no tuition-fee coverage. Foreign applicants must be admitted to a doctorate at a recognised university in Germany and prove German at C1, and applicants from developing or emerging countries are referred to the KAAD before applying to Cusanuswerk.
eligibility: Outstanding academic performance and interdisciplinary interest ('herausragende fachliche Leistungen und interdisziplinäres Interesse')
Pronounced social responsibility, voluntary engagement, creativity, openness and capacity for reflection

Membership in the Catholic Church; applicants of non-united Orthodox or Oriental Orthodox churches may apply on individual review; a lived Christian faith and willingness to co-shape the Church are required
Abitur or university entrance qualification entitling the applicant to study at a state or state-recognised university
German citizens: admission to doctoral study at a state-recognised university in Germany or abroad
Foreign applicants: admission to doctoral study at a state-recognised university IN Germany (funding of foreign doctoral candidates abroad is not possible) and German at level C1 minimum

Applicants from developing or emerging countries in Africa, Asia, the Near and Middle East, Latin America and Eastern Europe are referred to the KAAD first; a direct Cusanuswerk application is only possible in exceptional cases confirmed by KAAD
existing.eligibility_summary: Outstanding academic performance, interdisciplinary interest, social responsibility and voluntary engagement, membership in the Catholic Church with a lived Christian faith, university entrance qualification, and admission to doctoral study at a recognised university.
benefits: Doctoral stipend of EUR 1,750 plus EUR 100 research cost allowance
Health-insurance subsidy of 50% of premiums up to a maximum of EUR 170 per month where no compulsory statutory health insurance exists
Grants and advice for research stays abroad ('Förderung von Auslandsvorhaben')
Compatibility with 25% employment positions in science
coverage: Parent-independent doctoral stipend of EUR 1,750 (official wording: 'finanziell elternunabhängig in Höhe von insgesamt 1.750,00 Euro')
Research cost allowance of EUR 100 ('Forschungskostenpauschale in Höhe von 100,00 €')
No tuition-fee coverage is stated anywhere on the official doctoral funding page
requirements: Register online in the Cusanuswerk OmniBuS portal and upload the complete application package by the registration deadline
Submit an exposé of the doctoral project together with the application
Provide an academic teacher's reference (Hochschullehrergutachten); an English version of the reference template is published
Read the Merkblatt for the doctoral scholarship before applying
documents: Documents on academic performance ('Unterlagen zu Ihren fachlichen Leistungen')
Documents on personal career path ('Unterlagen zu Ihrem persönlichen Werdegang')
Academic teacher reference (Hochschullehrergutachten) — English template also published
Personal data form (Personalbogen) — published download on the official page
application_method: Online registration in the OmniBuS portal (https://omnibus.cusanuswerk.de/omnibus/register)
Upload of the complete application package electronically by the registration deadline
Upload window stays open for a few days after the registration deadline; late applications and late documents cannot be considered
Candidates already funded in the Cusanuswerk study funding scheme register informally via e-mail
existing.selection_notes: Applications undergo an internal review and a first pre-selection based on all submitted documents, which can take up to eight weeks; the final decision is then made by an interdisciplinary panel of university lecturers that also includes the Conference for Catholic University Chaplaincy (KHP) and the Cusanuswerk head office. Alumni of the Cusanuswerk study funding scheme have earlier internal deadlines (1 February for the spring round, 1 September for the autumn round).
existing.best_fit: Doctoral candidates who are members of the Catholic Church (or eligible Orthodox churches), already admitted to a doctorate at a recognised university, and seeking a parent-independent three-year stipend in Germany.
existing.notes: The official pages publish the doctoral funding details in German only; the German wording has been quoted rather than paraphrased.
existing.duration: Maximum funding period three years and six months, with additional extension options in cases of illness, maternity protection periods and child-rearing.
existing.application_period: Two annual selection rounds for external applicants: Verfahren I-2027 (Anmeldeschluss 1 November 2026, decision March 2027) and Verfahren II-2027 (Anmeldeschluss 1 June 2027, decision October 2027).
existing.deadline_display: Sunday, 1 November 2026 (registration deadline for Verfahren I-2027, selection decision March 2027)
existing.program_type: Foundation scholarship for doctoral candidates (church talent development body)
